summary: A tribute written in the style of a story, remembering Jon Postel, the long-time IANA leader who died in 1998. It is a personal memorial written by Vint Cerf and not a technical specification.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 2468 is Vint Cerf's remembrance of Jon Postel, who helped document Internet protocols and keep track of assigned names and numbers. Cerf describes Postel's service and proposes an award in his name.

questions: what did jon postel do for the internet
subtitle: Vint Cerf's remembrance of Jon Postel and his work for the Internet community.

tldr.problem: Jon Postel died in 1998 after decades of service to the Internet community.
tldr.mechanism: Vint Cerf's remembrance describes Postel's work as RFC Editor and IANA, his roles in Internet organizations, and his service to colleagues.
tldr.outcome: The memo proposes the Jonathan B. Postel Service Award and says Postel would be its first recipient, posthumously.

today: RFC 2468 is an Informational remembrance of Jon Postel. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Jon Postel's Work
sections.content: Vint Cerf's remembrance describes Jon Postel as the person who kept track of protocols, identifiers, networks, addresses, and names as the Internet developed. Postel became the RFC Editor when the Request for Comments series began and later volunteered to manage protocol identifiers, becoming IANA.
sections.plainLanguage: Postel edited early RFCs and managed Internet assignments of names and numbers. Cerf remembers him as a steady source of technical judgment and advice.

sections.title: Service to the Internet Community
sections.content: Cerf recalls meeting Postel at UCLA while they worked on the ARPANET project. The memo describes Postel's service on the Internet Architecture Board, as a trustee of the Internet Society, as custodian of the .US domain, and in other Internet roles. It also recalls his contributions to technical discussions and documentation.
sections.plainLanguage: The remembrance recounts Postel's work across several Internet organizations. It also describes his care for clear documentation and his colleagues.

sections.title: The Postel Service Award
sections.content: Cerf says that Postel completed the incorporation of a successor to his IANA service. As chairman of the Internet Society, Cerf pledges to establish the Jonathan B. Postel Service Award for long-standing service to the community and says Postel will receive it posthumously as the first recipient.
sections.plainLanguage: Cerf proposes an award for long-standing service to the Internet community. He says Postel will be its first recipient after his death.
